animals.diet: Carnivore – deer (chital, sambar), wild boar, gaur, water buffalo
animals.habitat: Tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests, mangroves (Sundarbans), grasslands
animals.ecological_role: Apex predator; regulates prey populations; keystone species maintaining forest health
interesting_facts: Largest subspecies of tiger
National animal of India and Bangladesh
Can swim up to 29 km
No two tigers have the same stripe pattern

animals.diet: Herbivore – grasses, leaves, bark, fruits, roots (200-300 kg/day)
animals.habitat: Savanna, woodlands, bushlands, and forest edges
animals.ecological_role: Ecosystem engineer; seed dispersal over vast distances; creates waterholes for other species; shapes vegetation structure
threats: Crop raiding leading to retaliation killings
interesting_facts: Largest land animal on Earth
Ears shaped like Africa
Can communicate via infrasound
Highly intelligent with long memory
Matriarchal social structure

animals.diet: Carnivore – blue sheep (bharal), ibex, argali, marmots, pika
animals.habitat: Alpine and subalpine zones; rocky terrain, steep cliffs; 3000-5500 m elevation
animals.ecological_role: Apex predator of high-altitude ecosystems; controls ungulate populations; indicator of healthy mountain ecosystems
conservation_measures: GSLEP (Global Snow Leopard Ecosystem Protection Programme)
interesting_facts: Cannot roar; makes chuffing sounds
Long tail used for balance and warmth
Paws act as natural snowshoes
Ghost of the mountains – rarely seen

animals.diet: Omnivore (99% bamboo) – eats 12-38 kg of bamboo daily; occasionally fish and small animals
animals.habitat: Temperate broadleaf and mixed forests with dense bamboo understory; 1200-3100 m elevation
animals.ecological_role: Seed dispersal; bamboo forest health maintenance; flagship conservation species
interesting_facts: False thumb (enlarged radial sesamoid bone)
Spends 10-16 hours eating daily
Cubs born blind and pink
National symbol of China
Symbol of WWF

animals.diet: Filter feeder – krill (up to 4 tonnes per day during feeding season)
animals.habitat: Open oceans; polar to tropical; deep pelagic zones
animals.ecological_role: Nutrient cycling (whale pump); maintains ocean productivity; top of marine food web
interesting_facts: Largest animal ever known to have existed (33 m, 190 tonnes)
Heart the size of a small car
Calls audible 1600 km away
Tongue weighs as much as an elephant

animals.diet: Carnivore – wildebeest, zebra, buffalo, giraffe, warthog
animals.habitat: Savanna grasslands, open woodlands, scrublands
geographic_distribution: Small population in Gir Forest, India (Asiatic Lion)
animals.ecological_role: Apex predator; controls herbivore populations; scavengers benefit from lion kills
interesting_facts: Only truly social cat; lives in prides
Roar audible up to 8 km
Females do 90% of hunting
Asiatic subspecies only 700 individuals remaining

animals.diet: Herbivore – grasses, leaves, branches, aquatic plants
animals.habitat: Floodplain grasslands, subtropical forest, wetlands in Himalayan foothills
animals.ecological_role: Grazer maintaining grassland structure; creates wallows used by other wildlife
threats: Poaching for horn (used in traditional medicine)
interesting_facts: Single horn made of keratin (like fingernails)
Can run up to 55 km/h
Excellent swimmers
Skin folds give armour-like appearance
Horn weighs up to 3 kg

animals.diet: Herbivore – leaves, shoots, stems, bark, roots, fruits
animals.habitat: Montane forests at 2200-4300 m elevation
animals.ecological_role: Seed dispersal; habitat modification through feeding; forest structure maintenance
interesting_facts: Shares 98.3% DNA with humans
Silverback males lead troops
Use tools and have cultural behaviours
First census showed fewer than 300 in 1980s – conservation success story

animals.diet: Carnivore – roe deer, sika deer, hares, badgers
animals.habitat: Temperate broadleaf and mixed forests with cold winters
animals.ecological_role: Apex predator in boreal ecosystem; controls deer populations
conservation_measures: Land of the Leopard National Park (Russia, 2012)
interesting_facts: Rarest big cat on Earth
Can leap 6 m horizontally and 3 m vertically
Unique spot pattern allows individual identification
Population down to ~30 in 2007; now ~100
sources: Land of the Leopard National Park

animals.diet: Omnivore – fruits (especially figs), leaves, bark, insects, small vertebrates
animals.habitat: Tropical lowland and montane rainforests of Sumatra
animals.ecological_role: Seed disperser for large-seeded tropical trees; shapes forest structure
threats: Deforestation for palm oil and pulp plantations
interesting_facts: Most arboreal great ape
Longest inter-birth interval of any mammal (7-9 years)
Uses tools (leaves as umbrellas, sticks for insects)
Distinct from Bornean orangutan since 1996
Shares 96.9% DNA with humans

animals.diet: Omnivore – seeds, insects, berries, small reptiles, plant parts
animals.habitat: Tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests, dry open forests, farmland
animals.ecological_role: Seed dispersal; insect population control; prey for large predators
conservation_measures: Protected under Indian Wildlife Protection Act 1972
interesting_facts: National bird of India
Tail (train) can be 60% of body length
Females prefer males with most eyespots
Can fly despite size
Named for iridescent plumage not actual colours (nanostructures)

animals.diet: Carnivore – fish, crustaceans, reptiles, birds, mammals; apex ambush predator
animals.habitat: Estuaries, mangroves, tidal rivers, coastal waters; tolerates full seawater
animals.ecological_role: Apex predator; nutrient cycling between marine and freshwater ecosystems
conservation_measures: Crocodile ranching programs reduce wild harvest pressure
interesting_facts: Largest living reptile (up to 6.17 m, 1000 kg)
Strongest bite force of any animal measured (~16,000 N)
Cannot chew – death rolls to tear prey
Survived mass extinction that killed dinosaurs

animals.diet: Carnivore – deer, pigs, goats, water buffalo, carrion; occasionally attacks humans
animals.habitat: Tropical savanna forests, grassland, scrubland of Indonesian islands
geographic_distribution: Indonesia (Komodo, Rinca, Flores, Gili Motang islands)
animals.ecological_role: Apex predator; scavenger maintaining ecosystem health; controls ungulate populations
predators: Large adult Komodo dragons cannibalize juveniles
conservation_measures: Komodo National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
interesting_facts: Largest living lizard
Venomous (anticoagulant venom)
Can reproduce parthenogenetically
Can detect carcasses 9.5 km away
Tongue is forked – detects chemical signals

animals.diet: Carnivore – primarily ringed and bearded seals; depends on sea ice for hunting
animals.habitat: Arctic sea ice, coastlines, tundra
geographic_distribution: Arctic Circle – Canada, USA (Alaska), Russia, Norway (Svalbard), Greenland
animals.ecological_role: Apex marine predator; nutrient transfer from sea to land
threats: Climate change – sea ice loss is primary threat
conservation_measures: International Agreement on Conservation of Polar Bears (1973)
Polar Bear management plans in range states
interesting_facts: Largest land carnivore
Fur appears white but is actually transparent
Black skin absorbs heat
Can swim 100 km continuously
Classified as marine mammals
Hybridizes with Grizzly Bears (Pizzly/Grolar Bear)

animals.diet: Carnivore – gazelles, impalas, rabbits, warthogs, birds
animals.habitat: Open savanna, grasslands, semi-arid scrubland
animals.ecological_role: Regulates prey populations; ecosystem balance in savanna
interesting_facts: Fastest land animal (112 km/h)
Semi-retractile claws for traction
Cannot roar; purrs, chirps, yelps
Only cat that cannot fully retract claws
Low genetic diversity due to ancient bottleneck

animals.diet: Herbivore – grasses, bark, roots, leaves, small stems (150-200 kg/day)
animals.habitat: Tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests, dry forests, grasslands
animals.ecological_role: Ecosystem engineer; seed dispersal; creates clearings; water source creator
interesting_facts: National animal of Thailand
Smaller ears than African elephants (shaped like Indian subcontinent)
Only males have tusks (unlike African species)
Capable of complex tool use and problem solving
Mourns dead companions

animals.diet: Carnivore – fish, shrimp, turtles; uses echolocation to hunt
animals.habitat: Freshwater rivers – Ganges, Brahmaputra, Karnaphuli-Sangu river systems
animals.ecological_role: Indicator species of river health; apex river predator; echolocation maps river bed
interesting_facts: Nearly blind – navigates entirely by echolocation
National Aquatic Animal of India
Functionally blind but detects light
Swims sideways in shallow water
Critically threatened flagship of Ganga restoration

animals.diet: Omnivore – seeds, insects, lizards, grass
animals.habitat: Dry grasslands and open scrubland of Indian subcontinent
geographic_distribution: India (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka)
animals.ecological_role: Indicator species of grassland health; seed dispersal; insect control
conservation_measures: Supreme Court of India order to underground power lines

Males can weigh 15 kg
Scheduled for extinction by 2040 without intervention
Once considered for India's national bird (peacock chosen instead)
sources: Supreme Court of India GIB Judgment 2021

animals.diet: Carnivore – jellyfish (primary diet); squid, sea urchins
animals.habitat: Open ocean pelagic; beaches for nesting
geographic_distribution: All tropical and subtropical oceans; nests on tropical beaches worldwide
animals.ecological_role: Jellyfish population control; nutrient cycling; beach nesting fertilises sand dunes
conservation_measures: Olive Ridley and Leatherback protection programs
interesting_facts: Largest sea turtle (2 m, 900 kg)
No hard shell – flexible leathery carapace
Can dive to 1200 m depth
Migrates 10,000 km between feeding and nesting
Maintained body temperature in cold water via counter-current heat exchange

animals.diet: Herbivore – grasses, herbs, shrubs of shola grasslands
animals.habitat: High-altitude grasslands (shola-grassland mosaic), rocky terrain at 1200-2600 m
geographic_distribution: India – Western Ghats (Tamil Nadu and Kerala)
Nilgiri Hills, Anamalai Hills, Periyar region
animals.ecological_role: Grazer maintaining grassland structure; prey for leopards and dholes
conservation_measures: Protected under Wildlife Protection Act India
interesting_facts: State animal of Tamil Nadu
Endemic to Western Ghats of India
Males have distinctively curved horns
Excellent rock climbers
Related to Himalayan tahr but genetically distinct

animals.diet: Larvae – Milkweed (Asclepias). Adults – nectar from various flowers
animals.habitat: Grasslands, meadows, open fields with milkweed; overwintering in oyamel fir forests
animals.ecological_role: Pollinator; indicator species for ecosystem health; important prey for birds
threats: Milkweed loss due to herbicide use
Deforestation of overwintering sites in Mexico
interesting_facts: Migrates up to 4000 km annually
Multiple generations complete one migration cycle
Toxic to predators due to milkweed alkaloids
Uses sun compass and Earth's magnetic field for navigation

animals.diet: Carnivore – hares, rabbits, ground squirrels, prairie dogs, marmots, birds
animals.habitat: Open and semi-open areas: mountains, hills, cliffs, open country
animals.ecological_role: Apex avian predator; controls small mammal and rabbit populations; indicator of open healthy ecosystems
conservation_measures: Protected under Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act (USA)
interesting_facts: National bird of Mexico, Albania, Germany, Austria
Wing span up to 2.2 m
Speed in stoop (dive) exceeds 300 km/h
Pair bond for life
Golden nape feathers give name
Used in traditional falconry for centuries

plants.habitat: Tropical dry forests, arid and semi-arid areas, degraded lands
plants.growing_conditions: Tropical climate, well-drained soil, full sun, drought-tolerant, grows at 0-700 m elevation
ecological_importance: Natural pesticide – reduces need for synthetic pesticides
Improves soil fertility
Air purification
Carbon sequestration
Provides habitat and food for birds and insects
Drought-resistant; grows in poor soils – reforestation tool
interesting_facts: Called Village Pharmacy in India
Every part is used: leaves, bark, seeds, fruit, roots
Neem oil in 700+ registered pesticide products globally
Used in Ayurveda for 5000+ years
UNESCO declared the Neem Tree of the 21st Century

native_region: South India (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh)
plants.habitat: Tropical dry forests, rocky terrain, 600-1000 m elevation; hemi-parasitic on host roots
plants.growing_conditions: Tropical climate, rocky or laterite soils, requires host plant (hemi-parasitic), moderate rainfall
medicinal_uses: Used in Ayurveda for urinary tract conditions
ecological_importance: Hemi-parasitic – dependent on host plants for nutrients
Supports pollinators
Fragrant wood important in cultural and religious rituals
Carbon storage
interesting_facts: One of the world's most expensive woods by weight
Heartwood takes 40-80 years to mature
Fragrance intensifies with age
Karnataka state tree
Protected by strict Karnataka government regulations
Used in Hindu and Buddhist ceremonies worldwide

plants.habitat: Tropical moist deciduous forests, rocky terrain, riparian areas, and urban environments
plants.flowering_season: Fruits February-May (not visible flowers – enclosed in syconium)
plants.growing_conditions: Tropical to subtropical, tolerates poor soils, grows on rock surfaces and walls, full sun
medicinal_uses: Bark used for skin diseases and wounds
Leaves used in Ayurveda for constipation
Root extracts for diabetes management in traditional medicine
ecological_importance: Hosts 200+ species of insects, birds, and mammals
Critical fig-wasp mutualism
Produces oxygen at night (CAM photosynthesis)
Sacred ecosystem – protected in villages
Carbon sequestration
Strangler fig – can colonise other trees
interesting_facts: Buddha attained enlightenment under a Peepal tree (Bodhi tree – same species)
Produces oxygen 24 hours (one of few plants)
Can live for thousands of years
Sacred in Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism
The Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi in Sri Lanka is 2300+ years old

plants.habitat: Tropical rainforest; obligate parasite on Tetrastigma vines; lowland and hill dipterocarp forests
plants.flowering_season: Unpredictable; flower blooms last only 5-7 days
plants.growing_conditions: Tropical humid rainforest, grows inside host vine with no leaves, stems or roots of its own
medicinal_uses: Limited; latex used in some traditional medicine for post-partum recovery in Borneo
ecological_importance: Pollinated by carrion flies attracted by corpse-like smell
Indicator of intact tropical forest
No chlorophyll – fully endoparasitic; uniquely evolved
Flagship for Sumatran and Bornean forest conservation
interesting_facts: Largest individual flower on Earth (up to 107 cm diameter, 11 kg)
Smells like rotting flesh to attract pollinators
Has no roots, stems or leaves – lives entirely inside host vine
Nicknamed the Corpse Flower
99% of buds never open
sources: Rafflesiaceae research – Royal Botanic Gardens Kew

plants.habitat: Shallow freshwater lakes, ponds, flooded fields, wetlands
plants.growing_conditions: Shallow freshwater (max 2.5 m), subtropical to tropical, full sun, muddy substrate
medicinal_uses: Leaves – treat heat stroke and diarrhoea
Rhizome – starch-rich food; treats respiratory and digestive conditions
Stamens – anti-ageing in traditional Chinese medicine
ecological_importance: Provides habitat for wetland species
Stabilises sediments
Oxygenates water
Key plant in Asian wetland ecosystem
Food and habitat for waterfowl and fish
interesting_facts: National flower of India and Vietnam
Self-cleaning leaves (Lotus effect – superhydrophobic surface)
Thermoregulates flower temperature to attract pollinators
Seeds viable for 1300 years (oldest germinated)
Symbol of purity in Hinduism and Buddhism

plants.habitat: Tropical and subtropical moist forests, riverbanks, urban environments
plants.growing_conditions: Tropical climate, wide range of soils, full sun; begins life as an epiphyte
medicinal_uses: Bark and leaves for diabetes management (traditional)
Latex for arthritis and skin conditions
ecological_importance: National tree of India
Hosts vast biodiversity – figs feed 60+ bird species
Aerial roots create microhabitats
Dense canopy provides shade ecosystem
Strangler habit shapes forest structure
interesting_facts: National tree of India
Thimmamma Marrimanu (India) – world's largest tree canopy (over 20,000 m²)
Starts as epiphyte on host tree, eventually strangles it
Can live thousands of years
Aerial prop roots become secondary trunks
Sacred in Hinduism – associated with Vishnu and Shiva

plants.habitat: Tropical moist forests, riverside locations, shaded areas in forest understorey
plants.growing_conditions: Tropical humid climate, deep loamy soil, partial to full shade, 500-1000 m elevation
medicinal_uses: Bark – treatment of uterine disorders and menstrual irregularities (Ashokarishta)
ecological_importance: Shade tree – supports forest understorey
Pollinators – visited by butterflies, bees and sunbirds
Culturally protected in many regions
Sacred – found in temple gardens across India
interesting_facts: One of the most sacred trees in South Asian religions
Named for Emperor Ashoka who planted it widely
Buddha's mother held its branch during his birth
Mentioned in Ramayana – Sita held captive in Ashoka grove
Overharvested for medicinal use – now considered vulnerable locally
Orange flowers are misidentified in popular culture

plants.habitat: Subtropical moist forests; specifically cypress swamps; grows on tree bark without leaves
plants.flowering_season: June-August (unpredictable; may not flower for years)
plants.growing_conditions: Subtropical climate, very high humidity, specific bark substrate, semi-shade; leafless plant
ecological_importance: Pollinated exclusively by Giant Sphinx Moth (Cocytius antaeus) – mutualist relationship
Indicator species of pristine swamp forest health
Part of complex mycorrhizal network
interesting_facts: Has no leaves or chlorophyll in juvenile/adult stage
Appears to float in air – roots photosynthesise
Rarely flowers – flowers last only a few days
John Laroche (The Orchid Thief) famously illegally collected this species
Featured in book 'The Orchid Thief' by Susan Orlean

plants.habitat: High plateau semi-arid regions; limestone surfaces; fog zone at 300-1500 m elevation
plants.growing_conditions: Arid to semi-arid; fog-dependent; limestone rocky terrain; extreme temperature range
medicinal_uses: Dragon's blood resin – wound healing and antimicrobial
Dye in traditional art and medicine
Used in traditional Socotri medicine for fever, diarrhoea
ecological_importance: Shapes the unique Socotra fog ecosystem
Resin provides habitat for insects
Endemic – found nowhere else on Earth wild
Umbrella canopy collects fog for soil moisture
interesting_facts: Red dragon's blood resin flows when bark is cut – name origin
Umbrella shape collects moisture from fog
Socotra (UNESCO World Heritage) called Galápagos of the Indian Ocean
Can live 600+ years
Tree appears prehistoric – unchanged for millions of years
Featured in NASA imagery of unique ecosystems

geographic_distribution: Namib Desert – coastal strip in Namibia and Angola only
plants.habitat: Hyper-arid Namib Desert; fog zone coastal strip; gravelly desert flats
plants.growing_conditions: Hyper-arid desert; coastal fog (main water source); extreme temperature; rocky desert substrate
medicinal_uses: Used by San people as emergency food (boiled)
ecological_importance: Living fossil – unchanged for 200 million years
Condenses fog moisture for surrounding desert biota
Supports rare desert invertebrates
Indicator of the unique Namib fog ecosystem
interesting_facts: Has only 2 leaves, grown continuously for its entire life (can exceed 1500 years)
Called the living fossil of the plant kingdom
Leaves can reach 8 m long, shredded by wind
Dioecious – separate male and female plants
Charles Darwin called it the platypus of the plant kingdom
Named after Friedrich Welwitsch who first documented it in 1859
sources: Kew Gardens – Plants of the World Online

geographic_distribution: Amazon Basin (Brazil, Bolivia, Colombia, Peru, Venezuela, Guyana)
plants.habitat: Shallow tropical rivers, oxbow lakes, backwaters of Amazon and Orinoco river systems
plants.flowering_season: Year-round in tropics; flowers last only 2 days
plants.growing_conditions: Tropical freshwater, warm temperatures, still or slow-moving water, high humidity, full sun
medicinal_uses: Traditional Amazonian people use leaves for skin conditions
ecological_importance: Provides platform habitat for wildlife
Large leaf surface aerates water
Supports complex food web of Amazonian wetlands
Seed dispersal by fish and birds
interesting_facts: Largest water lily leaves on Earth – up to 3 m diameter
Leaves can support weight of a child (up to 40 kg)
Flowers are thermogenic – heat up to 10°C above ambient
Pollinated by scarab beetles trapped inside flower overnight
Night-blooming white flowers turn pink on second day
Inspired the Crystal Palace greenhouse design (Joseph Paxton, 1851)

plants.habitat: Tropical dry forests, savanna, arid and semi-arid scrubland; rocky hillsides
plants.growing_conditions: Tropical and subtropical climate, well-drained sandy soils, full sun, drought-tolerant; loses leaves in dry season
medicinal_uses: Fruit pulp (baobab superfood) – high in Vitamin C (6x more than orange)
Leaves – treat fever and malaria in traditional medicine
Seed oil for cosmetics and skin care
ecological_importance: Called the tree of life – provides food, water, shelter
Hollow trunk stores up to 120,000 litres of water
Supports extensive biodiversity: bats, birds, insects, reptiles in trunk
Nitrogen fixation (symbiotic)
Critical resource for 200+ species in arid Africa
interesting_facts: Can live 3000+ years
Baobab in Limpopo, South Africa dated to 6000 years
Ancient trees are dying due to climate change
Called upside-down tree – bare branches look like roots
Fruit called monkey bread
Featured in The Little Prince by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
